record.original_question: Suppose a Costas array has the property that after adding one blank row at the top, every cyclic shift of the rows still yields a non-square array with the Costas property. Must the original Costas array be an exponential Welch W1 array?

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Let a Costas array have the property that, if a blank row is added at the top, then any cyclic shift of the rows leads to a (non-square) array with the Costas property. Is such a Costas array necessarily a W exp 1 array?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Costas array of order n is an n×n array with exactly one dot in each row and each column such that all the (n choose 2) vectors (difference vectors) connecting pairs of dots are distinct. More generally, an m×n array (with m ≠ n) is said to have the Costas property if it has at most one dot in each row and at most one dot in each column, and all difference vectors between pairs of dots are distinct.

For an odd prime p and a primitive root g modulo p, the exponential Welch construction W1 produces a Costas array A of order p−1 by placing a dot at row i and column j if and only if j ≡ g^{i-1} (mod p), for 1 ≤ i, j ≤ p−1.

Now let A be any Costas array of order n. Form the (n+1)×n array A' obtained by inserting a blank row above the first row of A. Consider all n+1 cyclic shifts of the rows of A' (i.e., for k = 0, 1, …, n, move the top k rows to the bottom in order). Suppose that every such cyclic shift yields an (n+1)×n array (necessarily non-square) that has the Costas property.

Question: Must A be (equivalent to) an exponential Welch W1 array?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a list of open problems on Costas arrays. Web search did not surface a published resolution characterizing exactly the Costas arrays for which adding a blank top row yields the Costas property under all cyclic row shifts. Recent works on Welch arrays with 1-gap rows discuss related structures but do not appear to settle this inverse characterization, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.claim: The inverse characterization of W1 via cyclic-shift Costas property of a blank-row extension is listed as an open problem.
